equity_bridge.item: CF Industries litigation settlement payable (agreed 15 Mar 2026, unpaid at balance date)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 note 11: A$247.3m recognised in other payables at 31 March 2026; a debt-like claim on the 31-Mar net debt. Deducted gross -- the significant-items table shows only 17.5 of tax on 274.6 of gross litigation cost, so little of it appears deductible.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: revenue_3yr_cagr (4.7%, FY22-FY25, includes the FY24 Cyanco and Terra Insights acquisitions) haircut toward the ~2.4% nominal growth of the global mining-explosives market plus price/mix from WebGen, Digital and cyanide; equals the base-case mid-horizon growth rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs are on STATUTORY EPS and are meaningless: FY22 (0.144) and FY25 (0.332) both carry hundreds of millions of significant items (Minova sale loss, LatAm impairment, litigation). Underlying EPS was 1.118 in FY25. Equity CAGR (4.5% 3yr) and revenue CAGR (4.7%) agree; FY20 5-year bases include the divested Minova business.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY19 260.4, FY20 -303.1, FY21 284.8, FY22 2.9, FY23 436.9, FY24 305.0, FY25 498.4. The 3-year and 5-year FCF CAGRs are undefined because the FY22 base (2.9, the Minova-exit and AN-cost-inflation year) and FY20 base (negative, 524 of capex on 277 of OCF) are not meaningful denominators; FY19-FY25 gives 11.4%. Reported-FCF and owner-FCF CAGRs do not diverge materially because SBC is only ~0.26% of revenue and interest income is small against the flows.

scenario_narratives.base: Orica is the global #1 in commercial explosives with a hazmat-regulated manufacturing and logistics moat, at a 13-year high in RONA. The base case takes FY26 guidance at face value (EBIT growth in every segment on flat revenue), lets the A$100m cost-out program add ~1pp of margin by FY28, then fades EBITDA margin from 19.9% to a 19.0% through-cycle level because gold at record prices and the cyanide/Digital growth engines are partly cyclical. Revenue compounds at 3-4% (market growth of ~2.4% plus price/mix and Digital/Chemicals share) fading to 2.5%. Capex and D&A converge at 5.3% of revenue; growth consumes trade working capital at 13% of incremental revenue. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF (about 6.5x EBITDA).
scenario_narratives.bull: Structural re-rating: Specialty Mining Chemicals (world's largest mining-dedicated cyanide producer) and Digital Solutions keep growing EBIT at 15-30%, gold and copper production growth sustains blasting volumes, WebGen wireless initiation takes share with pricing power reinforced by the Federal Court patent win over Dyno Nobel, and the cost-out program is fully retained. EBITDA (pre-SBC) reaches and holds 21% -- an EBIT margin near the FY2011-12 peak -- on 5-6% growth through FY29.
scenario_narratives.bear: The cycle turns: the CF Industries Yazoo City outage keeps US ammonium nitrate costs high through FY27, a gold/copper correction in FY27-28 shrinks volumes and premium mix, and margins revert to the FY24 level (EBIT ~10%) before only partially recovering. Recurring litigation and restructuring charges (A$274.6m in H1 FY26 alone) keep statutory cash conversion below underlying, and the A$2.2bn net-debt stack plus the A$247m CF settlement leave the equity to absorb the earnings fall. Value roughly halves against the base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on underlying (pre-significant-items) earnings, with SBC expensed and the share count held flat, leases charged as an operating cost with lease liabilities excluded from net debt, NCI folded into a 31% leakage rate calibrated to attributable underlying NPAT, and the unpaid A$247.3m CF Industries settlement deducted as debt. The margin path deliberately does not capitalise the FY26 peak: it lets the announced cost-out land and then fades toward a through-cycle level. Terminal value is capped at 15x owner FCF because the business is a moderate cyclical. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, against a single 9.0% AUD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin judgment: each 1pp of through-cycle EBITDA margin is worth roughly A$1.5-2/share; the market at ~8x EV/EBITDA is pricing FY26 margins as durable.
Ammonium nitrate supply: the CF Industries force majeure (no restart before Q4 2026) leaves US costs on the spot market until new supply contracts land.
Commodity exposure: ~26% gold, ~22% copper, ~23% coal of blasting revenue; a gold correction would hit both Blasting and the cyanide business at once.
Significant items have recurred every year (LatAm impairment, Minova, litigation); the model assumes they stop after the FY26 CF settlement and the A$50-60m of guided litigation cost.
Leverage: A$2.2bn net debt ex-lease (1.39x EBITDA) plus A$313m of leases; every A$100m of unexpected cash outflow is ~A$0.21/share.
Half-year timing: the 31 Mar 2026 balance sheet sits midway through the FY26 flow that is discounted as year 1; treated as a wash against the H1 dividend and buy-back.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 18.58-26.47.
data_sources.financials: ORI.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2016-FY2025, H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026); FY2025 Annual Report (underlying EBIT 992.2, D&A 498.9, lease principal 88.1 and interest 21.7, SBC 21.4, interest received 14.9, capex 414.5, OCF 949.2, buy-back 378.6, NCI 27.1, ETR 28.3%); H1 FY2026 Half-Year Report (net debt ex-lease 2,159.0 at 31 Mar 2026, cash 768.7, borrowings 2,927.7, lease liabilities 313.1, shares on issue 463.36m + 5.20m rights, underlying EBIT 512.0, CF Industries settlement payable 247.3, Nelson Brothers subsequent event).
data_sources.qualitative: ORI.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24): guidance, cost-out program, CF Industries force majeure, Dyno Nobel patent litigation, segment mix and commodity exposure.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payments expense' 21.4 (ORI.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:3964). Australian filer: awards settle by issuing deferred shares or on-market purchase (A$18.8m H1 FY26), no net-share tax withholding, so the combined figure equals the expense.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow A$378.6m on the up-to-A$500m on-market buy-back; a further A$139.4m in H1 FY2026 (A$101.1m buy-back cancelled at avg $24.06 plus employee-plan purchases). Buy-back completed 24 March 2026. The flat share count is therefore funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: 463,360,225 ordinary shares on issue at 31 March 2026 (H1 FY2026 note 7) plus 5,204,239 unvested performance rights (rights-over-unissued-shares table) = 468.6m fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging both would double-count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in AUD, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4%; ERP 5.5%; beta ~1.0 for a global mining-consumables supplier gives cost of equity ~9.9%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.7% (FY25 net interest ex-lease 178.0 on 2,668 of borrowings, USPP bonds), ~4.8% after tax. Market-cap weights ~79% equity / 21% debt give 8.8%; rounded to 9.0% for the emerging-market footprint (Latin America, Africa, Asia) that the beta does not fully carry. One WACC across all three scenarios; cyclicality, AN supply and litigation risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: FY2025 lease principal 88.1 (financing) + lease interest 21.7 (note 6c) = 109.8 = 1.35% of revenue, deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (313.1 at 31 Mar 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; net_debt 2,159.0 is Orica's own 'net debt excluding lease liabilities' (H1 FY2026 note 6a). D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY25 498.9 less ~88 ROU = 411, 5.0% of revenue; FY26 guidance 520-540 less ~90 ROU = 5.35%).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Non-controlling interests took 27.1 of FY25 underlying profit (~5% of attributable NPAT). The cash_tax_rate_path of 31% is the 28.3% underlying effective tax rate plus ~2.7pp of NCI leakage on EBIT, calibrated so FY25 NOPAT (970.5 x 0.69 = 669) ties to attributable underlying NPAT 541.1 + after-tax ex-lease financing 127.6 = 668.7. NCI equity (89.1) is NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the adaptations file applied: AUD-built WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI folded into the leakage rate, risk charged once. Orica is a mining-consumables manufacturer whose volumes track mining PRODUCTION (explosives are consumed per blast) more than capex, so it is a moderate rather than deep cyclical; FY25/H1 FY26 are a 13-year high in RONA and EBIT margin, so the base case lets the A$100m cost-out program lift margins through FY28 and then fades them toward a through-cycle level rather than capitalising the peak. Statutory earnings are ignored: FY25 statutory NPAT 162.3 carried 378.8 of significant items (LatAm impairment 264, litigation), H1 FY26 statutory was -0.6 after 274.6 of litigation costs; the build anchors on underlying EBIT 992.2 (FY25) and 512.0 (H1 FY26, +5%). EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC (Orica's underlying EBITDA is after SBC, so 21.4 is added back before the engine deducts it): FY25 = (992.2 + 498.9 + 21.4) / 8,144.5 = 18.6%. Share of associates' profit (59.7 FY25, Nelson Brothers JVs etc.) sits inside underlying EBIT, so the 358.2 of equity-accounted investments is NOT added in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Interest income 14.9 is stripped because the 768.7 cash pile is netted in the bridge. FY0 is FY2025 (last complete year); year 1 is FY2026, half of which had elapsed at the 31 Mar 2026 balance sheet -- the H1 FY26 owner cash generation already in that net debt roughly offsets the H1 dividend and buy-back cash out, so no further adjustment is made. Post-balance-sheet: Nelson Brothers JV buy-out (6 May 2026, US$25m cash + US$48m debt retired for 100% of the explosives JVs) is an asset bought at value and is not bridged. Deer Park Stage 2 land sale (guided to complete FY26) is an unquantified upside not credited. Price is the ASX regular close on the valuation date; not after-hours.

bear.rationale: FY26 EBIT growth is delivered but the CF Industries AN outage keeps North American costs elevated into FY27; a gold/copper price correction in FY27-28 cuts volumes and premium-product mix, taking EBITDA (pre-SBC) back to 16.5% (EBIT ~10%, the FY24 level) before a partial recovery to 18% (EBIT ~11%). Capex is cut to sustaining levels. Litigation and restructuring 'significant items' keep recurring. With A$2.2bn of net debt the equity absorbs most of the earnings fall.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +1%: H1 FY26 revenue was -1% (FX, Indonesia and US thermal coal softness) with guided EBIT growth coming from mix and margin, not volume. FY27-29 3.5-4%: gold/copper production growth plus Digital and Specialty Chemicals scaling and price/mix; fades to 2.5% nominal by FY33.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 19.6% in FY26 (underlying EBIT ~1,060 = +7%, inside 'growth across all segments', plus D&A guidance 520-540 and SBC), rising to 19.9% by FY28 as the A$100m cost-out program lands, then fading to a 19.0% through-cycle level from FY32 -- above the FY19-FY24 average (~17%) because Cyanco, Digital, WebGen mix and the LatAm restructure are structural, below the FY26 peak because RONA at a 13-year high is not a mid-cycle reading.
base.capex_da_rationale: FY26 capex 'broadly in line with 2025' (414.5 = 5.0%); thereafter 5.3% (FY23-25 average 5.5%) and D&A ex-ROU converges to the same 5.3%, so no persistent D&A-over-capex tax shelter is perpetuated.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: trade working capital (inventories 934 + trade receivables less trade payables 1,184) is ~13% of revenue, so growth consumes cash at 13% of the revenue change.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical; the method's 12-15x band); Gordon at 9.0%/2.5% is 15.8x so the cap binds. 15x FCF is ~6.5x terminal EBITDA versus ~8x EV/EBITDA today.

bull.rationale: Gold and copper capex cycle persists, Specialty Mining Chemicals and Digital keep compounding at 15-30% EBIT growth, the full A$100m cost-out is retained rather than competed away, and WebGen pricing power post the Dyno Nobel patent win lifts through-cycle EBITDA (pre-SBC) to 21% -- roughly a 14% EBIT margin, the FY2011-12 peak level. Growth capex runs higher (5.5%) to fund cyanide and emulsion capacity.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear weight up because the valuation is taken at a 13-year high in margins and RONA, gold is at record prices, the US AN supply contract is unresolved until September 2026, and significant items have recurred in each of the last three years. Bull weight down because the bull case needs three independent things to hold at once: the gold/copper cycle, full retention of the cost-out, and premium-product pricing power. Base at 50% because FY26 guidance is well underpinned by a record H1.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
